scope: interior pilot: habitat M interior, doorway (Blender compositions), provisional interior lighting

fixes: Break the clock face. 8 identical beds on 8 spokes read as a dial from the game camera. Group the beds into 4 bays of 2 (two beds side by side sharing one bedside unit), with a 1.2 m privacy screen (Frame edge + Cushion fabric panel) between bays. Keep the anchor numbers of V3 section 3.3; move the anchors with the beds.

Bed variety beyond blanket colour: 3 bed dressings (flat blanket; turned-down fold at the head showing a 25 cm white sheet; folded throw at the foot), 1 or 2 pillows, and a personal item (book, tablet, mug) on half of the bedside units. No two neighbouring beds the same.
Blankets are flat slabs. Give them a 3-4 cm rolled overhang on the sides and foot and a 1.5 cm bevel.

Industrial frontier cues inside (V3 7.1 asks for pipes): a two-pipe run (5 cm, Metal) along the wall above the skirting, 8 wall-top rib stubs (Frame, 8 x 8 cm) every 45 deg up to the cutaway height, 2 vent grilles. Halve the wood: wardrobes become a Hull/Frame carcass with wood door inserts. Now it reads as a hotel room, not a habitat.
Wall ring density: take out 1 wall item in 3 and show open wall (panel, a screen, a poster or a plant) so the ring has a rhythm instead of a solid band of cabinets; lower some items to 1.2 m.
Headboards are 0.96 m and face the camera on the near side: they hide the pillows in the cutaway (r2_rt_unsel_z7_y200.png). Lower to 0.80 m or make the top 30 cm a Cushion pad with the light strip.
Focal point: the table and rug are small for an M room. Rug radius 1.9 m, a table with an accent-coloured edge, and a planter or a light column at the centre.
Wall facets: add a 3 cm Frame batten at every segment joint so the 32 facet seams read as panels and the shading step is hidden.

Materials: the file has 25 materials, the contract says 14 per model. Orchestrator decision needed (the v2 exterior alone uses about 14). RENDER to measure draw calls for one room with merged visible segments.

Doorway against a headboard: at some link angles the door opens 0.8 m from the back of a headboard (habitat_m_doorways.png, left door; r2_crop_door_left.png). Make each bed headboard its own object Headboard_<i> and give RENDER a rule: hide it (or show a 0.6 m low variant) when a doorway centre is within 1.3 m. Target: >= 1.2 m clear floor in front of Anchor_Room at every angle.
Jamb clutter: the jamb is a stack of thin slabs and leaf slots (doorway_close.png, right jamb). One clean jamb profile, 12 cm deep, one recessed leaf slot, the green strip on the inner face only.

Outside (roof on): the collar header is a plain white box stuck on the dome (doorway_close_roof.png, habitat_m_doorways_roof.png). Chamfer 4 cm, a Frame trim line, continue the room's category stripe round the collar, 2 latch blocks; tuck its top under the dome's lower band.
Band break: wall_patch uses a Trim band, so the category band stops one patch before the frame and reads as a repair. Continue the category band on the patch and stop it at the frame.
Small rooms: the open leaves show up to 7 cm outside the outer wall at R <= 4 m. Shorten the travel or add pocket covers on the outer wall face.

RENDER, before the final rating (seen in its work in progress, build/web_sim 17:04): wall items of the cut segments show as cyan hologram fragments at the doorways, and frames overlap at the jambs (r2_crop_rt_doorL.png, r2_crop_rt_doorR.png). The same cyan flat fill shows on other wall items of the habitat (r2_rt_unsel_z7_y200.png, left shelf). A door must be clean in game: no fragments, no z-fighting, the wall hidden exactly across the frame.

Night: the warm-white floor goes navy and the beds sink into the dark (r2_rt_unsel_night_z7.png, ingame_habitat_m_night.png). Keep the night grade out of the cutaway interior, or add a per-room warm fill: an additive floor pool of radius 0.8 R, #FFE8C8, so the floor keeps >= 55% of its day brightness. V3 7.3: bright and readable by day and by night.
Real lights at Anchor_Light_* for the 2-4 rooms nearest the camera focus: ceiling 4500-5000 K, range 3.5 m; lamps warm 3000-3300 K with a small warm pool on the bedside unit and the pillow.
Cove strips light the wall: add a soft fake spill (a gradient quad 40 cm above the cove and 25 cm on the floor from the skirting strip) so the walls glow, not only the strip.

Blender night render (habitat_m_night.png) is the day render on a dark background. Re-render it as the target look: dim ambient, warm pools under the lamps and the 4 ceiling lights, glowing coves. RENDER then matches it.
By day the interior is good (r2_rt_unsel_z7_y200.png). Keep Screen at 0.45 and LightStrip out of the night emissive boost, as ART-HAB proposes.

notes: interior_habitat passes (0.73). In game close up it is readable, warm and tidy; the furniture is built to the NPC numbers (anchors checked with stand-ins) and matches the suit and building detail density. It is under 0.80 because of the radial repetition, the hotel-like wood finish with few frontier cues, and the dense cabinet ring.

doorways is a provisional pass (0.71) from the Blender compositions only. V3 section 9 asks for in-game shots of rooms with 1-4 corridors at odd angles; that evidence does not exist yet. The rating is final only after the in-game doorway is clean.
interior_lighting is a provisional fail (0.57), as expected: RENDER has not built the interior lights. Day is good; night is dim and cold.

Evidence gap: the coordinator said RENDER has not placed doorways. The newest build on disk (build/web_sim, 17:04, which carries the current presentation code) does place them; build/web_render was mid-export and had no index.html at 17:0x. I judged the doorway art on the Blender pictures and list the in-game faults for RENDER.
Seen in passing (npc_interaction, later round): colonists stand on beds and two overlap each other (r2_rt_unsel_z7_y290.png, right; r2_rt_unsel_z7_y200.png, top).
The cyan flat fill on wall items also appears in ART-HAB's own in-game shot with the room selected; I confirmed it with the room deselected, so it is not only the selection highlight.
full_delivery_must: Every room family in V3 section 9 at every size, built with the same kit, the same palette and detail density as habitat M after the fixes above; Blender renders art/interiors/<id>_<size>.png and in-game cutaway shots, day and night.

Doorways in game: rooms with 1, 2, 3 and 4 corridors at odd angles, day and night, close and at the game camera; no fragments, no z-fighting, doors slide when a colonist is within 2 m; >= 1.2 m clear floor inside every doorway.
Interior lighting in game: bright warm-white floors by day and by night, real lights near the focus, fake pools elsewhere, inside the performance budget of V3 section 0.2 (report fps and draw calls).
The material-count conflict (25 vs 14) resolved by the orchestrator and the draw-call cost of 32 wall segments measured.
